lessons: THRESHOLD RE-CONFIRMED, NOT CHANGED: the personal-import exemption is still USD 75 in July 2026. No new order since the USD 130 window ended on 1 June 2026. For a figure that moved four times in seven months, confirming it is the main job of the cycle.

CORRECTED the above-USD-500 band. The skill said 'full duty + VAT + purchase tax'. Kol Zchut says VAT applies and only SOME goods (וחלקם) additionally owe duty and purchase tax. As written the skill overestimated landed cost on every parcel in that band.

CORRECTED the USD 1,000 tier. The broker and rashimon requirement was stated as law; the source states only a tax consequence. Now framed as what carriers require in practice. Note the expert reviewer pushed back that this went too far and that simplified clearance really is capped by regulation. I could not source either direction (web-search budget exhausted), so the wording stays hedged and says to confirm with the carrier. Re-open this next cycle with a source.

REMOVED e-cigarettes from the exemption carve-out. The quoted exemption text names tobacco products and alcoholic beverages only. First draft of the fix still asserted that e-cigs are 'separately subject to purchase tax', which the judge caught as an unsourced affirmative liability; it is now a plain 'check the current rule'.

CORRECTED an internal contradiction on the VAT base: Step 2 said VAT applies to 'the product value' while the worked example and the script both correctly used CIF. The script was right. The two bases are now stated explicitly: the THRESHOLD is tested on goods value alone, the TAX on CIF plus duty plus purchase tax.

ADDED the 72-hour anti-splitting rule, verbatim-sourced. Two parcels from the same supplier to the same customer within 72 hours are assessed as one shipment. This answers the most common consumer workaround and was absent.

SCRIPT, four reproduced bugs: (1) a non-USD personal import silently lost the exemption because the threshold branch required currency == USD, so a EUR 50 parcel was taxed; it now requires --usd-value and refuses rather than guessing. (2) The threshold used strict less-than, so a parcel of exactly USD 75 was taxed although the rule is 'up to 75'. (3) --personal did not enforce the duty waiver in the 75-500 band, so a user who read a real duty rate off Shaar Olami was charged duty customs would not collect; the waiver is now enforced and reported. (4) A negative --fx produced a negative landed cost; inputs are now validated, including rates entered as 12 instead of 0.12.
SCRIPT: tobacco and alcohol exclusion existed only in the docstring, so a USD 50 bottle of whisky printed EXEMPT. Added --excluded-goods, which bypasses the exemption branch.

ADDED an explicit ad-valorem scope limit. The tariff uses specific (NIS per kg, per litre, per unit) and compound rates on food, beverages, alcohol, tobacco and some textiles, and neither the prose nor the script can express them. The skill now says so instead of implying every rate is a percentage.

PROCESS, the batch's recurring defect once more: the above-500 correction and the USD 1,000 downgrade landed in Step 2 but not in the Gotchas or the Step 1 table, and the superseded evidence claim tier-500-plus was left in place actively contradicting the new one. Old-value propagation has to include the summary tables, the gotcha list and evidence.json, not just the section that states the rule.

CARRY: purchase tax is computed on CIF plus duty plus a statutory uplift per tariff item (TAMA). The script omits the uplift and therefore understates exactly the shipments where purchase tax dominates. Not fixed because the uplift rates were not sourced this cycle.

CARRY: the FTA reference file was not touched this cycle and carries several unsourced specifics: the Canada CIFTA Form B239 four-year validity, the EU 6,000-euro invoice-declaration ceiling (which is load-bearing, it drives Example 3), the US Green Form discontinuation date, and the EFTA and Mercosur rows. The Canada citation reportedly does not contain the facts attributed to it.
CARRY: the EU-Israel settlement-goods exclusion from preferential treatment is missing entirely, and it is the most litigated origin rule on that agreement.

CARRY: release blockers are absent and matter more than tax for many parcels: standards approval, Ministry of Communications RF approval, and import licensing. Also absent: courier clearance and handling fees, which routinely exceed the tax on a small parcel, and the fact that customs may re-value a declared amount.
CARRY: 'VAT is recoverable' for commercial imports is true only where the rashimon is in the importer's own name and file number.

THRESHOLD RE-VERIFIED LIVE at USD 75 on 27 August 2026 against Kol Zchut. Every 'as of July 2026' stamp was refreshed; the Expert correctly flagged that a month-old stamp on the domain's most volatile figure is itself a defect.

CRITICAL FX DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: customs converts foreign-currency prices at the Bank of Israel representative rate PLUS 0.5 percent ('השער היציג של בנק ישראל בתוספת 0.5%'). Every landed cost the skill and the script produced was low by half a percent of CIF. The uplift is now stated once, in Step 5, and applied once, at CIF, in the script, which prints both rates so double-counting is visible.

CRITICAL EU-ORIGIN RETRACTION: the skill said the applicable rules were 'PEM 2012' and that 'Israel has not ratified revised PEM'. The European Commission country page says Israel signed the Regional Convention on 10 October 2013 and HAS ratified it, the Convention was established in 2011 not 2012, and the access2markets page says the two-set transitional regime ended 31 December 2025 with only the revised PEM applying from 1 January 2026. The skill was stating the opposite of its own cited source, and was stale by eight months. Found by the Independent Judge; verified by the orchestrator against both EC pages before encoding.

CRITICAL BOUNDARY CONTRADICTION: the prose said 'Below USD 75' while the source says 'עד 75 דולר' (up to and including) and the script implemented it inclusively. On a parcel of exactly 75.00 the skill and its own bundled script disagreed. Prose corrected to match source and script.

CRITICAL GAP CLOSED: the skill named an appeal against the assessment only to say where NOT to file it. The route is now stated: online through the personal area of the National Identification System, with proof of payment to supplier and evidence of actual transaction value, free of charge, tafag unit at the relevant customs house. The Eilat resident VAT refund uses the same route.

CARRY CLOSED (release blockers): Step 8 now names the competent authority per product class, including the 4-device threshold that moves a smartphone shipment out of the plain personal track and the helmet carve-out for EU or US certification.
CARRY CLOSED (courier fees, re-valuation): both are now sourced gotchas, along with the rule that a false declaration bites even a buyer who did not know.
CARRY CLOSED (VAT recoverable): qualified to the case where the rashimon is in the importer's own name and file number.
CARRY CLOSED (EU settlement-goods exclusion): added to the FTA reference with the Commission's own wording and the 2004 Technical Arrangement, flagged as running in the export direction.

CARRY CLOSED (FTA unsourced specifics): B239 confirmed against the CBSA form itself, which is titled 'Free Trade Agreement - Certificate of Origin (CIFTA only)' and carries a blanket-period field. The 'four years from signature' validity, the 1997 and 1 September 2019 CIFTA dates, the Green Form 10 January 2018 discontinuation date, the June 2000 EU entry-into-force and the June 2010 Mercosur date were all sourced to pages that do not state them, and are now explicitly withdrawn rather than silently deleted.

NEW: a whole refund entitlement was missing. Step 10 now carries the four conditions, the 6-month limit and the USD 250 export-inspection-form threshold, including the point people miss, that the shipper must record the refund intent on the export declaration at the time.

SCRIPT: --value abc raised a raw decimal traceback; argparse now rejects it cleanly. --excluded-goods no longer demands --usd-value it cannot use. The excluded-goods path now warns that alcohol and tobacco are on specific or compound rates the script cannot price at all, instead of printing a confident shekel figure on a rate the user invented. The exempt branch now says it excludes the clearance commission.

CARRY (re-logged, third cycle): the TAMA wholesale-price uplift rates are still not sourced. This cycle stopped pretending: the limit is now disclosed in Step 6, in the Hebrew mirror, in the script docstring and in the script's own output, and it is an explicit out-of-scope row in the new domain-checklist.md. Close it when a rate table is found.

CARRY (new): the EUR 6,000 invoice-declaration ceiling appeared seven times and drove Example 3 with no source anywhere. Both EC pages that would state it are JS shells that return no text. It is now hedged everywhere as unverified rather than asserted. Source it next cycle.

Expert CRITICAL deferred as OUT OF SCOPE (explicit, recorded in the new references/domain-checklist.md): ATA carnet and temporary import, goods returned after repair, toshav chozer, and diplomatic entry. The real harm the Expert identified was that the Step 1 table READ as exhaustive and routed those users into the commercial row. Step 1 now says it is not exhaustive, names each regime, and tells the user not to use the commercial row for them. Inventing procedures for four regimes I could not source would have been the worse answer.

Expert CRITICAL not encoded: 'the marketplace already collected VAT at checkout'. Plausible and probably common, but not stated on any source reachable this cycle, so Step 4.5 gives the procedural instruction (read the order confirmation for a tax line before computing) without asserting any platform's behaviour.
PROCESS: the documented command was `python scripts/...` on eight declared agents whose systems only ship `python3`. One character, in the only line a user copies. Found by the Expert.

PROCESS: I introduced a broken link myself by percent-encoding the Kol Zchut title without the quote character in מחו"ל. --check-sources caught it as a 404. Encoding a Hebrew page title by hand is a reliable way to fabricate a URL that looks right.

5.7 eval: the description change this cycle was a pure PREPEND of the legal clause ('Not customs advice.' / 'אינו ייעוץ מכס.') onto the SKILL.md and SKILL_HE.md frontmatter, which previously lacked it although metadata.json display_description had carried it since 1.3.0. No trigger phrase was removed, narrowed or reworded, so no holdout case can regress by construction. 10 frozen queries (6 positive, 2 negative, 2 edge), 3-query holdout, before 1.00, after 1.00, zero regressed.

Expert CRITICAL round 2, and the sharpest finding of the cycle: the alcohol and tobacco carve-out warning guarded the TAXED path and left the EXEMPT path silent, so a USD 50 bottle of wine printed a clean EXEMPT. That is the more likely input, and hardening the rarer path first is a pattern worth watching for. The exempt branch now always states the carve-out, and --excluded-goods with an ad-valorem purchase-tax rate is now refused outright instead of printing an invented figure.

Expert MINOR that was actually a correctness bug: the exempt branch was converting at the customs rate (representative plus 0.5 percent). The uplift belongs to a TAX base, and on an exempt parcel there is no tax, so the 'delivered cost' was overstated by half a percent for no reason. Now converted at the plain representative rate.

The domain-checklist justified keeping TAMA out of scope on the ground that its absence 'is disclosed at every point the purchase-tax line appears'. The Expert checked and it was not: duty-rates-by-category.md still published the bare formula. A checklist rationale is itself a claim and can be false.
